problems.title: Powers of a monomial
problems.question: Simplify[−(4/3)a³b²]²·(2a⁵b⁷)³.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: $(uv)^n=u^nv^n$; multiply like powers by adding exponents.
steps: The coefficient is(16/9)·8=128/9. Exponents are a:6+15=21, b:4+21=25.

problems.title: Add equations instead of solving prices
problems.question: Three churchkhelas and two breads cost14 GEL; one churchkhela and four breads cost18. Find the cost of two churchkhelas and three breads.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Let prices bec, n. Adding the equations gives 4c+6n=32.
steps: Divide by 2 to get2c+3n=16.

problems.title: Factor a difference of equal quadratic values
problems.question: Distinctx, y satisfy3x²−2025x=3y²−2025y. Find x+y.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
steps: Sincex≠y, the second factor is zero. Thus x+y=2025/3=675.

problems.title: Convert a total length to kilometres
problems.question: A broken line has five million segments, each 3–4 cm long. Which listed total is impossible?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Total length lies between15000000 and 20000000 cm;100000 cm=1 km.
steps: Thus the total is between150 and 200 km inclusive. Of149,159,169,179,189,199 km, only 149 is outside.

problems.title: Five points on one auxiliary circle
problems.question: ABCD is a parallelogram with acute A. H∈ray AB, K∈ray CB are different from B, CH=CB, AK=AB. If HDC=30°, find AKD.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Letα=angle DAB. The two isosceles triangles CBH, ABK give angles AHC=AKC=α. AlsoADC=180°−α.
steps: The second intersections H, K lie beyond B on their respective rays. The displayed equal/supplementary angles show A, H, C, D, K lie on the same circle.
AnglesAKD and AHD subtend the same chord AD, so they are equal. SinceAH∥DC, the angle AHD equals HDC=30°.

problems.title: Bounds of a linear expression
problems.question: Find the range ofk=3a−b for 2<a<5,−4<b<−1.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
steps: Adding gives 7<k<19.

problems.title: Cancel a common denominator but retain exclusions
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of(x²−4x)/[(x−5)(x+1)]=(x³+x²−29x)/[(x−5)(x+1)].
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Domain x≠5,−1. Equating numerators givesx³−25x=0.
steps: Factorx(x−5)(x+5)=0. Candidate roots are 0,5,−5.
Exclude5 because its denominator is zero. The remaining sum is −5.

problems.title: A symmetric rational identity
problems.question: Evaluate1/[(a−b)(a−c)]+1/[(b−c)(b−a)]+1/[(c−b)(c−a)].
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Use common denominator(a−b)(a−c)(b−c), for distincta, b, c.
steps: The three numerators are b−c,−(a−c), a−b. They sum to 0, so the expression is 0.

problems.title: Examples of inscribed triangles
problems.question: Which listed conditions can occur for an inscribed triangle:all sides<R; one side=2R; all sides<2R; all sides>R?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: A chord for a minor central angleθ has length 2Rsin(θ/2).
steps: Three points clustered within a short arc give all sides<R. A triangle on a diameter gives one side 2R.
An equilateral inscribed triangle has side √3R, which is both below2R and above R. Thus every listed condition is possible.

problems.title: Opposite side sums in a tangential quadrilateral
problems.question: A quadrilateral around a circle has sides in ratio2:3:5:x and perimeter112. Find its fourth side.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Tangency gives AB+CD=BC+DA, so 2+5=3+x.
steps: Thusx=4. The ratio sum is 14, so each unit is 8 and DA=4·8=32 cm.

problems.title: A square denominator determines integer ratios
problems.question: For positivex, y, which listedxy can make(4x−7y)/(5x²+45y²−30xy) undefined?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Denominator=5(x−3y)², so it vanishes exactly whenx=3y.
steps: Thenxy=3y². Among the listed values,12 works with y=2, x=6.
The other positive choices6,36 would requirey²=2,12, not integer squares.

problems.title: Bound a large power by taking a positive root
problems.question: Find the largest positive integern withn²⁵⁰≤5³⁷⁵.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Taking a 250th root givesn≤5^(3/2)=√125.
steps: Since11²=121≤125<144=12², the greatest integer is 11.

problems.title: Factor before expanding four factors
problems.question: How many integer roots has(x+2022)(x+2023)(x+2024)(x+2025)=(x+2024)(x+2025)(x+2026)(x+2027)?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
steps: The bracket is −8x−16196, whose zero is −2024.5, not an integer.
The two remaining roots are −2024 and −2025.

problems.title: Check a median problem whose options do not match
problems.question: BK is a median, KBA=70°, BKC=140°. Find the largest-minus-smallest angle of ABC.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: BKA=40°, so BAK=70° and AB=BK. ScaleAK=KC=1 and place K=(0,0), A=(−1,0), C=(1,0).
steps: WriteB=t(cos140°, sin140°). The equality AB=BK givest=1/(2cos40°), hence B=(−1/2, tan40°/2).
Largest minus smallest is 110°−2arctan(tan40°/3)≈78.7474°.
problems.answer: Approximately78.7474°; none of the listed choices.
problems.note: The printed70° and 140° conditions lead to this value. The listed20°,30°,40°,45°,60°,70° do not match.

problems.title: A repeated side length in an obtuse isosceles triangle
problems.question: ABC is isosceles with B=120°. D lies onray AB with BD=2AB. IfAC=12, find CD.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: LetAB=BC=s. SinceD is beyond B, angle CBD=60°.
steps: The cosine rule gives AC²=2s²−2s²cos120°=3s².
AlsoCD²=s²+(2s)²−2s·2s·cos60°=3s². ThusCD=AC=12.

problems.title: Compare reciprocal terms with positive denominators
problems.question: Positive integersm, n satisfy(m−5)/m<(n−5)/n. Which listed relation is impossible?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Write1−5/m<1−5/n. This gives 1/m>1/n, so m<n.
steps: The relationm=3n contradictsm<n. The other options can occur for suitable positive integers.

problems.title: Use the branch specified by the question
problems.question: For(x−3)/(x+2)−(2x+1)/|1−x|=(−x²−8x−15)/[(x+2)(x−1)], find the digit sum of its root above3.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: For x>3,|1−x|=x−1 and both denominators are nonzero.
steps: Multiplying by(x+2)(x−1) gives(x−3)(x−1)−(2x+1)(x+2)=−x²−8x−15.
The left side is −x²−9x+1, so x=16. Its digit sum is 1+6=7.

problems.title: Square the given ratio
problems.question: Given(a²+2b²)/(ab)=4, find(a⁴−2a²b²+4b⁴)/(a²b²).
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: The square of the given expression has numeratora⁴+4a²b²+4b⁴ and value16.
steps: The requested numerator is smaller by 6a²b². After division, the answer is 16−6=10.

problems.title: Midlines of two sub-trapezoids
problems.question: A tangential trapezoid has legs3,5. Its midline splits it into trapezoids whose midlines have ratio5:11. Find the base difference.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Tangency gives base suma+b=8. The sub-midlines are(3a+b)/4 and(a+3b)/4.
steps: Set11(3a+b)=5(a+3b), givingb=7a. Witha+b=8, the bases are 1 and 7.
Their difference is 6.

problems.title: A perpendicular median-foot segment in a right triangle
problems.question: In right triangle ABC, K is midpoint of hypotenuse AB, M∈AC with AM:MC=2:1, and MK⊥AB. IfAC=24, find MK.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
steps: Perpendicular direction vectors MK=(4, b/2), AB=(−24, b) have dot product 0, so −96+b²/2=0.
ThusMK²=4²+b²/4=16+48=64, and MK=8.

problems.title: Combine neighbouring strict gaps
problems.question: The numbersa,2a, b,11.89 increase, with each neighbouring gap below3. Which listedb is possible?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: The first gap gives 0<a<3, so 2a<6 and b<2a+3<9. The final gap givesb>8.89.
steps: Only 8.99 lies in(8.89,9) among the choices. It is attainable with a=2.999:the three gaps are 2.999,2.992,2.9.

problems.title: Multiply a congruence by an inverse
problems.question: Integersx, y satisfy5x−16y divisible by 29. Which listed expression must also be divisible by 29?
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: The inverse of 5 modulo29 is 6, because5·6=30≡1.
steps: Thusx≡6·16y=96y≡9y modulo29. Consequently9y−x is divisible by 29.

problems.title: Quadratic terms cancel in a system
problems.question: Findx+y if(x−3)²+4y=x²+7 and(x−2y)(x+2y)−4xy+5x+8y²=(x−2y)²+y+11.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Expanding and cancelling gives 3x−2y=1 and 5x−y=11.
steps: The second givesy=5x−11. Substitute into the first:3x−10x+22=1, so x=3, y=4.
Thusx+y=7.

problems.title: Three isosceles triangles in a right trapezoid
problems.question: Join the midpoint M of a right trapezoid’s longer leg to its vertices, forming three isosceles triangles. The shorter leg is one triangle’s base. Find the acute trapezoid angle.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: Let parallel bases bea>b, and perpendicular legh. ThenMA=MB=U, MC=MD=V and U²−V²=ab>0.
steps: The two other isosceles triangles have sides(a, U, V) and(b, U, V). Sincea>b and U>V, the equalities must bea=U, b=V.
Let the acute trapezoid angle beθ. The large-base triangle has equal base anglesθ, so its apex angle is 180°−2θ.
At the upper-left right angle, the other part is therefore180°−2θ. The small-base triangle gives that same angle asθ/2.
Solve180°−2θ=θ/2 to obtainθ=72°.

problems.title: A bisector fixes the base-length ratio
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, the obtuse B-bisector meets base AD at its midpoint M; N is midpoint of BC, and AB=BC. FindMN:BD.
problems.idea: Simplify the algebra or identify the equal angles and lengths that control the figure.
formulas: BecauseBC∥AD, the bisector makes triangle ABM isosceles, so AM=AB=BC=s and AD=2s.
steps: PutA=(0,0), D=(2s,0), B=(u, v). Thenu²+v²=s², M=(s,0), N=(u+s/2, v).
ThusMN²=(u−s/2)²+v²=5s²/4−su, while BD²=(u−2s)²+v²=5s²−4su=4MN².
ThereforeBD=2MN and the ratio is 1:2.
